answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond on the cedar registry and files one pigment waste manifest. The spiral ledger publishes manifests once, and the disposer signs a receipt. An auditor recomputes ledger against receipts and burns the bond on a missing, reused, or mismatched manifest. A forger pays 80 plus a fee per fake identity; slots fill, so the k-th costs 35+5(k-1), the 1,000th 5,030, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,532,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-disposal ring fails: one disposer signs at most three per epoch, and a shared receipt burns both bonds. An honest agent pays once.
